learning_outcomes.text: Students can design mechatronic systems, solve manufacturing tasks by applying Rapid Technologies through understanding mechatronic processes, and apply knowledge of manufacturing electronic printed circuit boards.

Students can implement a given or self-developed concept into a design, dimension and shape mechanical components, manage a development or design task in a team, communicate within the team and clarify interfaces to carry out product development within the process chain "task clarification to manufacturing release".

Students master the process chains of Rapid Technologies from 3D digitization to additive manufacturing processes and can apply them in development processes. They understand the basics of developing and manufacturing printed circuit boards and their use in packaging and interconnection technology, as well as the assembly, soldering, and testing procedures in the production of flat assemblies and can apply these in the design of mechatronic systems.

syllabus_topics: Task clarification and requirements modeling
Function analysis with creation of the functional structure
Derivation and evaluation of principle solutions
Conception, dimensioning, and design of components and assemblies
Stress-compliant, manufacturing-compliant, assembly-compliant design
Application of components
Concept implementation in a design exercise task
Basic processes of "Printed Circuit Board Technology" and "Packaging and Interconnection Technology"
Development and manufacturing processes of single-layer and multi-layer printed circuit boards (PCB = Printed Circuit Boards)

Development and production of assembled printed circuit boards, so-called flat assemblies (FBG), both for mounting through-hole devices (THD = Through Hole Device) and for mounting surface-mounted devices (SMD = Surface Mounted Device)
Special designs (e.g., Multi-Chip-Modules MCM, Flip-Chip)
Assembly processes and testing procedures (manual for prototype construction and machine for series production)
Components and common connection technologies, such as wave soldering and reflow soldering alongside alternative soldering processes (partial soldering, stamp soldering, inert gas soldering, etc.)
Process chains for Rapid Technologies
Processes and tools for Rapid Prototyping, Rapid Manufacturing, and Rapid Tooling
Data formats and interfaces
Properties and classification of additive manufacturing processes
Physical and technological principles for additive manufacturing
Devices and processes for generation from liquid, solid, and gaseous phases
3D digitization
Current research projects in the field of Rapid Technologies

assessment_methods.method: Constructive Semester Project, attestations for the results of the development phases (unweighted course achievement)
graded written exam (45 min) or graded presentations (20 min) for MECB452
graded written exam (45 min) or graded presentations (20 min) for MECB453

assessment_rules: The module grade for MECB450 is composed of MECB452 and MECB453, weighted equally according to CP. MECB451 involves unweighted study achievements (Testate).
